auth_model.login:
ENDPOINT: POST /api/auth/login — defined routes/auth_routes.py:117-147 (router prefix "/api/auth" at line 75).

CONTENT TYPE: application/json (Pydantic body model `LoginRequest`, routes/auth_routes.py:35-39). NOT form-encoded. Fields: `username` (str), `password` (str), `remember` (bool, default True), `totp_code` (str, optional). Username is .strip().lower()'d server-side (auth_routes.py:122).

FLOW: verify_password first (auth_routes.py:123 → core/auth.py:374-378, bcrypt). If the account has TOTP enabled and no totp_code is sent, it returns HTTP 200 {"ok": false, "requires_totp": true, "username": ...} (auth_routes.py:126-131) — you must re-POST with totp_code. Bad password/code → HTTPException 401 "Invalid credentials" / "Invalid 2FA code".

SUCCESS RESPONSE: HTTP 200 JSON {"ok": true, "username": "<lowercased>"} (auth_routes.py:147).

SESSION COOKIE: name `odysseus_session` (the constant SESSION_COOKIE, routes/auth_routes.py:71). Set at auth_routes.py:136-146 with httponly=True, samesite="lax", path="/", secure = (env SECURE_COOKIES=="true", default false). max_age=604800 (7 days) ONLY when remember is true (default true); otherwise a session cookie. Value is secrets.token_hex(32) → 64 hex chars (core/auth.py:385). Sessions persisted to data/sessions.json, TTL 7 days (core/auth.py:41,380-392). Logout: POST /api/auth/logout revokes the token and deletes the cookie (auth_routes.py:149-155).
auth_model.csrf:
NO CSRF TOKEN EXISTS. A full grep for "csrf" across the codebase (*.py) returns zero matches — there is no CSRF token issued, no header/field to carry one, and no endpoint to obtain one. No request requires a CSRF token.

CSRF defense relies entirely on the cookie's SameSite=Lax attribute (routes/auth_routes.py:140) plus CORS (app.py:67-84, allow_credentials=True, origins from ALLOWED_ORIGINS, default http://localhost,http://127.0.0.1).

For a black-box tester: state-changing requests (POST/PUT/DELETE) need ONLY the session cookie (or a Bearer API token). Do not add any X-CSRF-Token / csrf field — none is validated. There is also no X-Requested-With enforcement (it is merely listed as an allowed CORS header, app.py:81).
auth_model.middleware:
AuthMiddleware defined app.py:216-323, only registered when AUTH_ENABLED != "false" (default enabled, app.py:135,140).

PUBLIC/EXEMPT (app.py:141-157, _is_auth_exempt): EXACT paths = /api/auth/setup, /api/auth/signup, /api/auth/login, /api/auth/logout, /api/auth/status, /api/auth/features, /api/auth/settings, /api/auth/integrations/presets, /api/health, /api/version, /login. PREFIX exempt = /static (also note /backgrounds page is served without auth, app.py:732-735). Everything else requires auth.

UNAUTHENTICATED RESPONSES (app.py:311-316): if path starts with "/api/" → HTTP 401 JSON {"error": "Not authenticated"}; otherwise (page loads) → 302 RedirectResponse to /login. First-run (no users configured): non-API → 302 /login, API → 401 {"error": "Setup required"} (app.py:250-254).

AUTH ORDER per request: (1) exempt check; (2) internal-tool token bypass; (3) LOCALHOST_BYPASS; (4) Bearer API token; (5) cookie session.

LOCALHOST/INTERNAL BYPASSES:
- LOCALHOST_BYPASS env (default false, app.py:136). When true, any DIRECT loopback request bypasses auth entirely (app.py:248-249). "Trusted loopback" = client.host in {127.0.0.1, ::1} AND none of these proxy headers present: cf-connecting-ip, cf-ray, cf-visitor, x-forwarded-for, x-forwarded-host, x-real-ip, forwarded (app.py:195-214). So spoofing X-Forwarded-For DISABLES the bypass, not enables it.
- Internal-tool token (app.py:225-240): header X-Odysseus-Internal-Token matching core.middleware.INTERNAL_TOOL_TOKEN (env ODYSSEUS_INTERNAL_TOKEN, else random per-process, core/middleware.py:16-17) AND trusted loopback → bypasses auth, sets current_user="internal-tool" (which require_admin treats as admin, core/middleware.py:33). Optional X-Odysseus-Owner header impersonates an existing user for ownership attribution (app.py:233-238). /api/internal/* routes additionally gate on this same token (routes/internal_routes.py:30-37).

Note: NOT exempt from the separate 45s hard-timeout middleware (app.py:114-128) except whitelisted streaming prefixes.
auth_model.admin:
TWO mechanisms, both ultimately reading users[username]["is_admin"] from data/auth.json via auth_manager.is_admin() (core/auth.py:247-248).

1. Auth routes (routes/auth_routes.py): each admin route resolves the user from the cookie via _get_current_user() (auth_routes.py:81-83) then checks `if not user or not auth_manager.is_admin(user): raise HTTPException(403, "Admin only")`. Examples: GET/POST/DELETE /api/auth/users (249-250, 256-257, 347), PUT /api/auth/users/{u}/privileges (268), .../rename (279), /signup-toggle (338), POST /api/auth/features (364), POST /api/auth/settings (391), all /api/auth/integrations* mutations (410,426,437,448,459). GET /api/auth/settings returns scrubbed (secret-blanked) settings to non-admins, full to admins (auth_routes.py:376-385).

2. Other route modules: helper require_admin(request) from core/middleware.py:20-45. It reads request.state.current_user (stamped by AuthMiddleware) and calls auth_mgr.is_admin(user). IMPORTANT bypasses inside require_admin: (a) returns immediately (allow) if env AUTH_ENABLED=="false" (middleware.py:39); (b) allows if X-Odysseus-Internal-Token matches, or current_user=="internal-tool" (middleware.py:29-36). Used by e.g. POST/DELETE /api/tokens (api_token_routes.py:50,83), admin-wipe routes, etc.

Bearer API-token callers get current_user="api" (a literal string, never an admin) so is_admin("api") is False → they cannot reach admin routes.
auth_model.api_tokens:
HEADER + FORMAT: `Authorization: Bearer ody_<token>`. Handled in AuthMiddleware app.py:256-309. Only an Authorization value starting with the literal "Bearer ody_" is treated as an API token (app.py:258); anything else falls through to cookie auth. After stripping "Bearer ", the raw token must be 12–100 chars (app.py:261). Tokens are generated as "ody_" + secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (≈43 url-safe chars), routes/api_token_routes.py:56. First 8 chars (token_prefix, e.g. "ody_xxxx") index an in-memory cache; the full token is bcrypt-verified against stored hash (app.py:263-278). On match: request.state.current_user="api", api_token=True, api_token_id, api_token_owner, api_token_scopes (DB scopes, default ["chat"]) (app.py:300-304). Invalid token → 401 JSON {"error": "Invalid API token"}.

CREATION (admin only): POST /api/tokens with form field `name` (Form-encoded, not JSON), api_token_routes.py:48-79 — returns the raw token ONCE in {"token": "ody_..."}. List: GET /api/tokens; revoke: DELETE /api/tokens/{id} — all require_admin (api_token_routes.py:22,83). Default scope is "chat" (api_token_routes.py:14; DB column core/database.py:412).

WHICH ROUTES ACCEPT THEM: the bearer check runs globally in AuthMiddleware, so a valid token authenticates ANY non-exempt route (operating as pseudo-user "api"; owner-scoped data uses api_token_owner). The ONLY purpose-built token endpoint is POST /api/v1/chat (routes/webhook_routes.py:195-202, router prefix "/api"), which hard-requires request.state.api_token is True AND "chat" in api_token_scopes, else 403. Admin routes remain closed (is_admin("api") is False). No X-API-Key / X-Auth-Token inbound auth exists — those appear only in CORS allow_headers (app.py:77-78) and are used for OUTBOUND LLM provider calls, not to authenticate to Odysseus.
auth_model.rate_limit:
LOGIN limiter: RateLimiter(max_requests=15, window_seconds=60) — routes/auth_routes.py:77, checked at auth_routes.py:119-120. Keyed by request.client.host (caller IP). Exceeding 15 requests in any rolling 60s window → HTTPException 429 "Too many requests — try again later".

NO LOCKOUT / NO ESCALATION: it is a pure in-memory sliding-window counter (src/rate_limiter.py:26-39), per-IP, in-process only (not persisted, resets on restart). It does NOT distinguish success vs failure — every POST /api/auth/login counts, and there is no per-account lockout, no exponential backoff, no captcha. Once the window drains below 15, requests are allowed again immediately.

Related limiters (same RateLimiter class): signup = 3 req / 300s (auth_routes.py:78,102), setup = 3 req / 300s (auth_routes.py:79,88). Login attempts are also subject to 2FA gating but TOTP failures still consume from the 15/60s budget.

TESTER CAVEAT: the key is request.client.host with no X-Forwarded-For trust (no ProxyHeaders middleware). Behind a reverse proxy/tunnel all clients share the proxy's IP bucket; on direct localhost every attempt is keyed to 127.0.0.1.
auth_model.tester_notes:
To script authenticated curl requests:

COOKIE AUTH (recommended): POST JSON to /api/auth/login, e.g. `curl -c jar.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"USER","password":"PASS"}' http://HOST/api/auth/login`, then reuse with `-b jar.txt`. The cookie is `odysseus_session`. No CSRF token, no X-Requested-With needed. If the account has 2FA, the first call returns {"requires_totp": true}; re-POST adding "totp_code". Username is lowercased server-side.

BEARER AUTH: `-H 'Authorization: Bearer ody_...'` works on any non-admin route; the dedicated scoped endpoint is POST /api/v1/chat (JSON body {"message": ...}). Tokens must be admin-created (POST /api/tokens, form field name=). Cannot reach admin routes.

NO WEBSOCKETS: grep for websocket/WebSocket returns nothing. Streaming chat uses SSE/HTTP (e.g. /api/chat, /api/shell/stream) authenticated by the same cookie/Bearer — no separate WS handshake auth to handle.

NO USER-AGENT GATING: no inbound User-Agent checks exist (only outbound scrapers set UA). Any/empty UA is fine.

OTHER GOTCHAS:
- Cookies: secure flag is off by default (SECURE_COOKIES=false), so plain HTTP works for testing; SameSite=Lax.
- CORS: allow_credentials=True with origins from ALLOWED_ORIGINS (default http://localhost,http://127.0.0.1). Cross-origin browser calls from other origins are blocked, but curl ignores CORS.
- 45s hard request timeout returns 504 for non-whitelisted paths (app.py:100-128); long jobs under /api/chat, /api/research, /api/upload, /api/image, /api/model/* etc. are exempt.
- Public (no-auth) endpoints usable for probing: /api/health, /api/version, /api/auth/status, /api/auth/features, /api/auth/settings (scrubbed), /api/auth/integrations/presets, /login, /static/*, /backgrounds.
- First-run: if no users exist, everything redirects/401s until POST /api/auth/setup creates the first admin (password min 8 chars).
- Two privileged backdoors to be aware of when interpreting results: LOCALHOST_BYPASS=true (direct-loopback, no proxy headers → full bypass) and the X-Odysseus-Internal-Token header (loopback-only, grants admin-equivalent + X-Odysseus-Owner impersonation). Sending any of cf-connecting-ip/x-forwarded-for/x-real-ip/forwarded/cf-ray/cf-visitor/x-forwarded-host DISABLES the loopback trust path.
- Files cited: app.py (middleware/bearer/bypass), routes/auth_routes.py (login/logout/admin), core/auth.py (AuthManager/sessions/TOTP), core/middleware.py (require_admin/internal token), routes/api_token_routes.py (token CRUD), routes/webhook_routes.py:195 (/api/v1/chat), src/rate_limiter.py, src/auth_helpers.py (require_user/require_privilege/owner_filter).

endpoints.purpose: Danger Zone: truncate one whole data domain. kind in {chats, memory, skills, notes, tasks, documents, gallery, calendar}
endpoints.test_plan: With an admin session, pick the least-coupled kind: curl -X DELETE -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/admin/wipe/notes. Expect 200 {"status": "deleted", "kind": "notes", "count": <N rows before delete>}. Each of the 8 kinds returns the same shape. Fixture: optionally create one note first so count>=1 proves the truncate. RUN LAST in any test pass — each kind drops ALL rows for that domain (not owner-scoped): chats wipes Session+ChatMessage tables and clears the session_manager in-memory cache; memory truncates Memory table, blanks data/memory.json, removes memory_tidy_state.json and clears the chroma vector store; skills rmtree's data/skills/ and removes legacy skills.json; tasks deletes TaskRun then ScheduledTask; documents deletes DocumentVersion then Document; gallery deletes GalleryImage rows and rmtree's data/gallery + data/gallery_uploads; calendar deletes CalendarEvent then CalendarCal.
endpoints.bad_input: DELETE /api/admin/wipe/bogus -> 400 "Unknown wipe kind: 'bogus'". Non-admin session -> 403 'Admin only'.
endpoints.notes: Global (all-users) wipe, no confirmation parameter, no undo. Kind is case-insensitively normalized. DB errors roll back and return 500. Wiping 'chats' invalidates every session_id fixture other tests hold; 'memory'/'skills' also delete on-disk files.
endpoints.result: created throwaway note then DELETE /api/admin/wipe/notes -> 200 {status:'deleted', kind:'notes', count:1}. Bad kind /wipe/bogus -> 400 'Unknown wipe kind'. Valid kinds: chats,memory,skills,notes,tasks,documents,gallery,calendar.

Then: curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:PORT/api/agents/<agent_id>/files' (optional query ?path=subdir). Expect 200 {"path": "", "entries": []} — workspace_root() creates the folder on demand, so an empty entries list is the valid fresh-agent happy path. Entries have {name, is_dir, size, mtime} sorted dirs-first.

endpoints.purpose: Read one text file from the agent's sandbox, path-confined and capped at 200,000 chars

Expect 200 {"path": "hello.txt", "name": "hello.txt", "size": <bytes>, "mtime": iso8601Z, "binary": false, "truncated": false, "content": "<file text>"}. Binary: ?path=binfile.bin -> binary:true, content:"". Bad inputs: omit path -> 422 missing-field validation; ?path=missing.txt -> 404 'File not found'; ?path=../../../etc/passwd -> 400 'Path is outside the workspace'.

Matches auth_routes.py:213-222 + core/auth.py:316-335.

endpoints.purpose: Admin connectivity test: publishes a real ntfy message, or GETs a preset health endpoint (miniflux /v1/me, gitea /api/v1/version, linkding /api/tags/, homeassistant /api/, default /)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie + an integration whose base_url points at a REACHABLE service. Easiest hermetic happy path: create integration {"preset":"ntfy","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8091"} with a local ntfy running, then POST /api/auth/integrations/<id>/test with empty body. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Sent to http://127.0.0.1:8091/reminders — ..."}. Without a reachable backend the endpoint still returns 200 but {"ok":false,"message":"...failed..."} — assert on the ok field, not the status code.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown integration id -> 404 "Integration not found"; non-admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Real outbound HTTP side effect: for ntfy it POSTs an actual notification to the topic from settings key reminder_ntfy_topic (default 'reminders') — subscribers WILL receive a test message. base_url path/query is stripped to scheme://host:port for ntfy. Other presets go through execute_api_call (uses stored api_key + auth_type). 8s httpx timeout for ntfy. Network failures are reported as ok:false with a 200, never 5xx.
endpoints.result: No ntfy backend listening on 127.0.0.1:8091 (verified: connection refused). POST /744fec880fd8/test, empty body -> 200 {ok:false, message:"ntfy publish to http://127.0.0.1:8091/Reminders failed: All connection attempts failed."} — clean graceful error, no 5xx/traceback/hang, asserts on ok field per design (auth_routes.py:499-525). Topic correctly pulled from settings reminder_ntfy_topic="Reminders". Bad input: unknown id -> 404 {detail:"Integration not found"}. No real notification sent (no server/subscribers).

endpoints.purpose: Password (+ optional TOTP) login; sets the odysseus_session cookie

Expect 200 {"ok":true,"username":"admin"} and a Set-Cookie header for odysseus_session (httponly, samesite=lax, max-age 604800 when remember=true). If the user has 2FA enabled and totp_code omitted, expect 200 {"ok":false,"requires_totp":true,"username":"admin"} — then retry with "totp_code":"123456".

Wrong-password 401 path (lines 122-124 raise 401 "Invalid credentials") NOT exercised to honor the shared one-login/15-per-min budget; verified by code read.

endpoints.purpose: Revoke the current session token and clear the session cookie

Form fields: message, session, mode (chat|agent), attachments (JSON array string), use_web, use_research, use_rag, time_filter, preset_id, allow_bash, allow_web_search, search_context, compare_mode, incognito, no_memory, active_doc_id; header x-tz-offset stashes user TZ. mode=agent runs the full tool loop (bash/python/file tools unless disabled) and may bind to a crew/claude_code engine; use_research=true starts a multi-minute background research job (LONG-RUNNING path) with progress events; image-model sessions route to image generation. endpoints.purpose: Upload a PDF (multipart) and create a Document from it — form-backed markdown if AcroForm fields exist, else plain PDF doc with pdf_source marker
endpoints.test_plan: curl -X POST /api/documents/import-pdf -F 'file=@sample.pdf' (optional -F 'session_id=<owned-session-uuid>'). Needs a real PDF file fixture. Expect 200 with doc dict (id, title from filename, current_content containing a pdf_source/upload marker, version_count>=1). Requires can_use_documents privilege and a configured upload_handler.
endpoints.bad_input: session_id of a nonexistent session -> 404 'Session not found'; missing file field -> 422.
endpoints.notes: Multipart upload. Saves the file via upload_handler (persists in uploads dir, owner-stamped). For AcroForm PDFs it also writes a field-schema sidecar file next to the upload. Text extraction uses pypdf; pages with images and <50 chars of text trigger a vision-LLM OCR call (analyze_image_with_vl) — a plain text PDF makes no LLM call, a scanned PDF does. Subject to the global 45s REQUEST_HARD_TIMEOUT? No — path starts with /api/upload exemption does NOT apply; /api/documents/import-pdf is NOT timeout-exempt, so big scanned PDFs may 504.
endpoints.result: POST multipart -F file=@sample.pdf -F session_id=<owned> -> 200 doc dict: title='audit_tmp_sample' (from filename), language markdown, current_content starts with '<!-- pdf_source upload_id="...pdf" -->' marker + extracted text, version_count=1. Plain text PDF (177 chars, no images) -> NO LLM/OCR call. Also tested no session_id -> 200 library doc (session_id null, owner stamped). Bad inputs: session_id=fake -> 404 'Session not found'; missing file field -> 422. Minor cosmetic content bug (not a failure of intent): document_routes.py:187 uses `.lstrip("\n[PDF content]:")` which is a charset strip, so '[Page 1 text]:' is mangled to 'age 1 text]:' in the body. Endpoint still fulfills its purpose.

endpoints.purpose: Same-origin proxy for OpenMoji monochrome line-art emoji SVGs, lazily fetched from jsdelivr CDN and disk-cached
endpoints.test_plan: Logged-in session: curl -b cookies.txt http://HOST/api/emoji/1f600.svg -> 200 Content-Type image/svg+xml. With network to cdn.jsdelivr.net: real glyph body containing '<svg', header Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; cached to data/emoji_cache/1f600.svg so a second call serves from disk (works offline thereafter). Multi-codepoint form also valid: /api/emoji/1f468-200d-1f469-200d-1f467.svg.
endpoints.bad_input: Invalid code (e.g. /api/emoji/zzz!.svg) or unknown codepoint -> STILL 200 with a blank 1x1 transparent SVG and Cache-Control: no-store — this endpoint never 404s.
endpoints.notes: Outbound HTTPS to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net (8s timeout) only on cache miss; offline first-fetch degrades to blank SVG, not an error. Code must match ^[0-9a-f]{2,6}(-[0-9a-f]{2,6})*$ (lowercased). No per-route auth; gated by global AuthMiddleware.
endpoints.result: GET /api/emoji/1f600.svg -> 200 image/svg+xml, 955B real OpenMoji glyph ('<svg id="emoji" viewBox="0 0 72 72"...'), header Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable. Multi-codepoint /api/emoji/1f468-200d-1f469-200d-1f467.svg -> 200, 4328B real glyph. Both written to data/emoji_cache/ (verified on disk -> serves from disk thereafter). Bad input /api/emoji/zzz!.svg -> 200, 64B blank 1x1 transparent SVG, Cache-Control: no-store (never 404s, matches code _BLANK_SVG path). Network to cdn.jsdelivr.net reachable so real glyphs returned.

endpoints.purpose: Localhost-only in-process tool execution proxy for per-agent Claude Code sessions (runs any Odysseus agent tool with full runtime state)
endpoints.test_plan: Must be called from 127.0.0.1 with NO proxy-forwarding headers and header X-Odysseus-Internal-Token: $ODYSSEUS_INTERNAL_TOKEN (set this env var before starting the app for a deterministic token; otherwise it's random per process). Optionally X-Odysseus-Owner: <existing username> for owner attribution. POST JSON {"tool": "bash", "args": {"command": "echo internal-ok"}}. Expect 200 {"ok": true, "result": <tool output containing 'internal-ok'>}. Unknown tool e.g. {"tool":"nope"} -> 200 {"ok": false, "error": "Unknown or invalid tool: nope"}.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing/wrong X-Odysseus-Internal-Token (with valid admin cookie) -> 403 'forbidden'; non-JSON body -> 400 'invalid json body'; JSON without 'tool' -> 400 'tool required'
endpoints.notes: Double auth gate: AuthMiddleware in app.py validates token + trusted loopback (rejects if any of cf-connecting-ip/x-forwarded-for/etc. headers present) and sets current_user='internal-tool' or impersonated owner; the route re-checks the token (constant-time). Tool execution failures return 200 {ok:false,error}. Body also accepts session_id and workspace_root. Executes real tools (bash/python/web_search/email/MCP-namespaced mcp__server__tool) — pick harmless args.
endpoints.result: From plain loopback (no forwarding headers) with X-Odysseus-Internal-Token + X-Odysseus-Owner: admin, body {"tool":"bash","args":{"command":"echo internal-ok"}} -> 200 {"ok":true,"result":{"output":"internal-ok","exit_code":0}}. Without owner header the route still runs (ok:true) but bash self-restricts since owner='internal-tool' is not admin. {"tool":"nope"} -> 200 {"ok":false,"error":"Unknown or invalid tool: nope"}. Bad inputs: missing token WITH admin cookie -> 403 {"detail":"forbidden"} (route defense-in-depth, internal_routes.py:38); wrong token no cookie -> 401 (middleware); non-JSON body -> 400 {"detail":"invalid json body"}; JSON w/o tool -> 400 {"detail":"tool required"}.

Bad inputs: transport=stdio no command -> 400 'command is required for stdio transport'; transport=sse no url -> 400 'url is required for SSE transport'. Fixture deleted afterward.

endpoints.purpose: Create (or dedupe-return existing) model endpoint; optionally probes for models; may auto-set global default chat endpoint

Expect 200 {"id": "<8-char uuid>", "name": "test-ollama", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1", "models": [], "online": false, "status": "offline"|"online"|"empty", "ping_error": ...}. Re-POST same base_url returns the existing row with "existing": true (dedupe). Cleanup: DELETE /api/model-endpoints/{id}.

Side effects: strips /models|/chat/completions|/v1/messages suffixes, resolves hostname via Tailscale helper, probes network (1-3s) unless skip_probe=true, and if settings.json has no default_endpoint_id it SETS default_endpoint_id/default_model globally. shared=false stamps owner=caller. Invalidates model caches.

Re-POST same base_url -> 200 same id with "existing":true (dedupe). Bad input: omit base_url -> 422 Field required; base_url="" (literal empty form value) -> 422 missing (FastAPI treats empty Form value as not-provided); whitespace/strippable base_url (e.g. "   " or "/models") -> 400 "Base URL is required". default_endpoint_id NOT overwritten (already set, so auto-set branch skipped). Fixture deleted afterward.

endpoints.bad_input: Empty/missing query -> 200 {"context":"","sources":[],"error":"query is required"} (never 4xx).

All failures are wrapped into a 200 envelope with 'error'. Subject to the global 45s request timeout. _request_values deliberately accepts JSON, form, and query params.
endpoints.result: POST /api/search {"query":"latest python release"} -> 200 {"context":<3977 chars>,"sources":[5]} with NO error key (happy path; primary searxng@localhost:8080 unreachable so provider chain fell back to duckduckgo and returned real results). Bad input: {"query":""} -> 200 {"context":"","sources":[],"error":"query is required"} (never 4xx, by design); no cookie -> 401 from middleware. (routes/search_routes.py:46-66)

endpoints.purpose: Create a new chat session; optionally validates the model against the endpoint's /v1/models, or binds the chat to an agent (crew member).
endpoints.test_plan: Form-encoded (not JSON): curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://HOST/api/session -d 'name=Test Chat' -d 'skip_validation=true'. Expect 200 SessionResponse: {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "Test Chat", "model": "", "rag": false, "archived": false}. With skip_validation=true no network probe happens, so no live model endpoint is needed.
endpoints.bad_input: POST with no endpoint_url and no skip_validation -> 400 'endpoint_url is required (choose from /api/models)'. crew_member_id=nonexistent -> 404 'Agent not found'.
endpoints.notes: Without skip_validation it probes endpoint_url's /v1/models over the network (400 'Cannot reach /v1/models' on failure, 400 'Model not found at server. Available: ...' on mismatch). With crew_member_id of a claude_code agent it REUSES the agent's existing non-archived session instead of creating one (returns that session's id). Fires 'session.created' webhook and 'session_created' event-bus event. endpoint_id form field resolves a stored ModelEndpoint API key into session headers.
endpoints.result: POST /api/session -d 'name=audit-tmp-s' -d 'skip_validation=true' -> 200 {"id":"7c071deb...","name":"audit-tmp-s","model":"","rag":false,"archived":false}. Bad input: no endpoint_url + no skip_validation -> 400 {"detail":"endpoint_url is required (choose from /api/models)"}; crew_member_id=nonexistent-xyz -> 404 {"detail":"Agent not found"}.

endpoints.purpose: Create a session pre-wired to api.openai.com using the server's OPENAI_API_KEY.
endpoints.test_plan: Requires OPENAI_API_KEY set in server env (.env). Form-encoded: curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://HOST/api/session/openai -d 'model=gpt-4o'. Expect 200 {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "", "model": "gpt-4o"}. No outbound call is made at creation time, but the key must be configured.
endpoints.bad_input: Server without OPENAI_API_KEY -> 400 'Server missing OPENAI_API_KEY'.
endpoints.notes: Session endpoint_url hardcoded to https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with Bearer header. Fires session_created event. Name form field is accepted but ignored (session saved with name '').
endpoints.result: POST /api/session/openai -d 'model=gpt-4o' -> 400 {"detail":"Server missing OPENAI_API_KEY"}. Clean 4xx, no stack trace/hang. OPENAI_API_KEY is commented-out in /Users/clawdio/odysseus/.env so the guard at session_routes.py:764 fires as designed (EXTERNAL-CREDS class).

endpoints.purpose: Summarize older messages into one compacted system entry via an LLM call (session_routes version — WINS over the shadowed history_routes handler at the same path).
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: own session with >= 6 messages (inject 8 via inject_messages) AND a reachable utility/default model endpoint (or working session endpoint+model). curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://HOST/api/session/<sid>/compact. Expect 200 {"ok": true, "summarized": N, "kept": M, "message_count": K} where kept is min(8, max(4, len//4)).
endpoints.bad_input: Session with < 6 messages -> 400 'Not enough messages to compact'.
endpoints.notes: Consumes LLM tokens (utility endpoint preferred, falls back to the session's own endpoint; 400 'No model configured for compaction' if neither). LLM timeout is 60s but the route is NOT in the app's hard-timeout exempt list, so a slow model can trip the global 45s 504 (REQUEST_HARD_TIMEOUT). Rewrites history: [summary system msg] + recent tail. The richer history_routes compact handler (keep-4, hidden system summary, before/after token pct) is shadowed and never runs. NOTE: operates on sess.endpoint_url -> legacy/sidecar only; behavior on agent-bound (empty endpoint_url) sessions to verify in round 2.
endpoints.result: 6-message session -> {"ok":true,"summarized":2,"kept":4,"message_count":5}

endpoints.purpose: Report the model's real context window length by querying the session's endpoint.
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: own session. curl -b cookies.txt http://HOST/api/session/<sid>/context_info. Expect 200 {"context_length": <int>, "model": "<model>"} when the endpoint is reachable, or {"context_length": null} for sessions without endpoint/model or on any probe failure (never errors).
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown sid -> 404 (from owner check).
endpoints.notes: Makes a network call to the session's model endpoint via src.model_context.get_context_length; degrades gracefully to null. Not an LLM completion — no token spend.
endpoints.result: GET /api/session/<sid>/context_info on endpoint-less/model-less fixture -> 200 {"context_length":null} (matches session_routes.py:1176-1177: returns null when no endpoint_url/model; never errors). Bad input: unknown sid -> 404 {"detail":"Session nonexistent-xyz not found"} (owner check). No LLM completion.

endpoints.purpose: Delete specific messages by DB id (msg_ids) or legacy positional indices.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new session containing a copy of the first keep_count messages of the source.
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: own session loaded in memory with >= 2 messages. curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://HOST/api/session/<sid>/fork -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"keep_count": 2}'. endpoints.bad_input: Session not present in the in-memory manager (only in DB) -> 404 'Session not found'.
endpoints.notes: Uses session_manager.sessions.get() directly (no DB lazy-load), so a session evicted from memory 404s even though it exists. Fork inherits endpoint_url/model/owner, rag=False. Fires session_created event. keep_count defaults to 0 (empty fork).
endpoints.result: POST .../fork {"keep_count":2} on in-memory session w/4 msgs -> 200 {"status":"ok","id":"d368421c...","name":"⫝ audit-tmp-fork","kept":2}; GET history of new id shows 2 copied messages. endpoints.purpose: Star/unstar a session to protect it from deletion and auto-cleanup.

endpoints.result: ?skip_llm=true cheap path -> 200 {status:ok, updated:0, folders:[], deleted_empty:0, deleted_throwaway:0, unfiled_remaining:0, skipped_llm:true}. (LLM full path is the same handler with folder naming; skip path exercises the deterministic cleanup.)

Bad input: {} (missing command) -> 422 body.command Field required. Admin-gated via _require_admin.

endpoints.purpose: Execute a shell command streaming output line-by-line over SSE; optional PTY mode and tmux background mode
endpoints.test_plan: POST JSON {"command": "echo one; echo two", "timeout": 30} with admin session, Accept: text/event-stream. Expect 200 text/event-stream with events like data: {"stream":"stdout","data":"one"} ... terminated by data: {"exit_code": 0}. PTY variant: add "use_pty": true (POSIX only). tmux variant: {"command":"echo bg","use_tmux":true} -> first event announces 'Started tmux session: cookbook-xxxxxxxx', then output lines, then exit_code event.

Default timeout 120s; timeout:0 = run until client disconnects. tmux mode requires tmux binary, survives disconnect (background job semantics), writes wrapper script + log under $TMPDIR/odysseus-tmux/ (log cleaned up on completion). use_pty on a platform without pty support yields error event with error:'pty_unsupported' and exit_code -1.
endpoints.result: POST {"command":"echo one; echo two","timeout":30}, Accept text/event-stream -> 200 text/event-stream: data: {"stream":"stdout","data":"one"} / data: {"stream":"stdout","data":"two"} / data: {"exit_code":0}. Empty command {"command":""} -> 200 SSE data: {"stream":"stderr","data":"No command provided"} then {"exit_code":1} (not an HTTP error). PTY (use_pty) and tmux (use_tmux) variants not exercised (POSIX sub-features); core pipe-streaming contract verified.

endpoints.bad_input: DELETE /api/tokens/nonexistent -> 404 'Token not found'.
endpoints.notes: Pairs naturally with the create test (create -> list -> delete -> 404 on re-delete).
endpoints.result: DELETE /api/tokens/8129579e -> 200 {"status":"deleted"}; subsequent GET /api/tokens no longer lists it; re-DELETE same id -> 404 {"detail":"Token not found"}. Bad input (nonexistent id) covered by the re-delete 404.

endpoints.purpose: List all agent tool tags with enabled/disabled status from settings
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/tools with any logged-in session. Expect 200 {"tools": [{"id": "<tool-tag>", "enabled": true}, ...]} sorted by tag; tags listed in settings.disabled_tools come back enabled:false.
endpoints.notes: No handler-level auth (middleware-only). Reads src.agent_tools.TOOL_TAGS + settings.json.
endpoints.result: GET /api/tools (admin) -> 200 {"tools":[{"id":"adopt_served_model","enabled":true},...]} sorted by id, built from src.agent_tools.TOOL_TAGS + settings.disabled_tools (model_routes.py:1450-1459). After POST disabling web_search, GET reflected {"id":"web_search","enabled":false}; after restore it showed enabled:true. No-auth -> 401 (middleware-only, no handler gate).

endpoints.purpose: Set the global disabled-tools list
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. POST /api/tools with JSON {"disabled": ["web_search"]} → 200 {"ok": true, "disabled": ["web_search"]}. Verify GET /api/tools now shows web_search enabled:false. Restore with {"disabled": []}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"disabled": "web_search"} (string not list) → 422 pydantic validation error.
endpoints.notes: Writes settings.json globally — affects all users' agent runs; restore original value after testing.
endpoints.result: POST {"disabled":["web_search"]} (admin) -> 200 {"ok":true,"disabled":["web_search"]}; GET /api/tools then showed web_search enabled:false. Restored with POST {"disabled":[]} -> 200 {"ok":true,"disabled":[]}; GET showed web_search enabled:true and load_settings()['disabled_tools']==[]. Bad input: {"disabled":"web_search"} (string) -> 422 list_type 'Input should be a valid list'. Auth: POST without cookie -> 401 (require_admin).

endpoints.purpose: Clear the TTS synthesis cache
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/tts/clear-cache with empty body and a logged-in cookie. Success: 200 {"success": true, "message": "Cache cleared"}.
endpoints.bad_input: No auth cookie -> 401. (No request-body validation — any body is ignored.)
endpoints.notes: Side effect: deletes cached audio files; harmless and idempotent. Safe to run anytime.
endpoints.result: POST /api/tts/clear-cache (empty body) -> 200 {"success":true,"message":"Cache cleared"}. Idempotent/harmless. No cookie -> 401.

endpoints.purpose: Report TTS service provider/availability statistics
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/tts/stats with a logged-in cookie. Success: 200 JSON with {"available": bool, "ready": bool, "provider": ...} plus model/cache details.
endpoints.bad_input: No auth cookie -> 401.
endpoints.notes: Default tts_provider is 'disabled' -> available:false but still 200.
endpoints.result: GET /api/tts/stats -> 200 {"available":false,"ready":false,"provider":"disabled","model":"tts-1","voice":"alloy","speed":1.0,"cache_entries":0,"cache_size_mb":0.0} — matches default disabled provider. No cookie -> 401.

endpoints.purpose: Synthesize speech from text via the configured TTS provider (local Kokoro or API endpoint), returning audio bytes or base64
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: tts_provider set to 'local' (Kokoro-82M loaded) or 'endpoint:<id>'. Request: POST /api/tts/synthesize JSON {"text": "Hello world", "format": "base64"}. Success: 200 {"audio": "<base64 string>"}. With format "audio" (default): 200 binary body, Content-Type audio/mpeg or audio/wav, Content-Disposition inline. On default install (disabled) expect 503 — record as expected-unavailable.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing 'text' -> 422 (pydantic). Provider disabled/browser -> 503 {"message": "TTS service not available"}. Synthesis returning nothing -> 500 {"message": "Synthesis failed"}.
endpoints.notes: Caches results keyed by provider/model/voice/text. Local Kokoro requires model + GPU/CPU runtime; first synthesis can be slow and /api/tts is not exempt from the 45s hard timeout. format values other than 'base64' fall through to binary audio.
endpoints.result: tts_provider=disabled (default; no Kokoro/endpoint configured). POST /api/tts/synthesize {"text":"Hello world","format":"base64"} -> 503 {"detail":{"message":"TTS service not available"}} — clean error, no hang/traceback (route short-circuits on tts_service.available, tts_routes.py:34-38). Bad input: missing 'text' -> 422 pydantic. Cannot exercise real synthesis without TTS provider runtime/creds.

endpoints.purpose: Upload one or more files (multipart) with sanitization, dedupe, type/size checks; returns metadata per file
endpoints.test_plan: With a logged-in session cookie: curl -b cookies.txt -F 'files=@test.png' http://HOST/api/upload  (form field name must be 'files'; repeat -F for multiple). Expect 200 {"files":[{"id":"<32-hex>.png","name":"test.png","mime":"image/png","size":N,"hash":"...","uploaded_at":"...","width":W,"height":H,"is_duplicate":false}]}. The id matches ^[0-9a-fA-F]{32}\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$ and is the fixture for the GET/vision endpoints.
endpoints.bad_input: Upload a file named evil.exe (or an empty 0-byte file) -> 400 'File type not allowed: ...' / 400 'File is empty'. Sixth upload within 60s from same IP -> 429 'Upload rate limit exceeded'.
endpoints.notes: Rate limits: 5 uploads/min/IP, max_concurrent_uploads=3 (429), max size 10MB (400). Dedupes by SHA hash per owner (is_duplicate=true returns existing id). Files stored under UPLOAD_DIR/YYYY/MM/DD, index in UPLOAD_DIR/uploads.json with owner=current user. Blocked extensions: .exe .dll .bat .cmd .vbs .ps1 .jsp .asp .aspx.
endpoints.result: POST -F files=@audit-tmp.png (real 1x1 PNG) -> 200 {"files":[{"id":"aaf965e307cb4ce692c0918e5c6550e0.png" (matches ^[0-9a-fA-F]{32}\.png$),"name":"audit-tmp-red.png","mime":"image/png","size":70,"hash":"c414cd...","width":1,"height":1,"is_duplicate":true}]} -- dedupe correctly matched an identical pre-existing admin-owned PNG (per-owner SHA dedupe, code lines 470-501). Bad input -F files=@evil.exe -> 400 'File type not allowed: application/x-msdownload' (python-magic detected). Rate limit 5/min & max 3 concurrent (code) NOT stress-tested to protect the IP-shared upload budget; counter increments before validation so each attempt costs a slot.

endpoints.purpose: Manually trigger deletion of uploaded files older than 30 days
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session, no body: curl -X POST -b admin_cookies.txt http://HOST/api/upload/cleanup -> 200 {"status":"success","files_cleaned":0} (0 on a fresh install). Non-admin session -> 403 'Admin only'.
endpoints.notes: Side effect: permanently deletes uploads older than cleanup_days=30. Safe on fresh test data (nothing >30d old) but do not run against a long-lived instance you care about.
endpoints.result: Admin: POST /api/upload/cleanup -> 200 {"status":"success","files_cleaned":0}. Safe-verified before running: cleanup_old_uploads compares the YYYY/MM/DD dir name (2026/06/10) against now-30d (2026-05-11); 2026-06-10 is not older, so 0 deletions. Auth gate: unauthenticated -> 401; require_admin raises 403 for non-admin (code, not exercised - no non-admin session).

endpoints.purpose: Return aggregate statistics about uploaded files
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session: curl -b admin_cookies.txt http://HOST/api/upload/stats -> 200 JSON stats dict from upload_handler.get_upload_stats() (file counts/sizes). Works with zero uploads. Non-admin -> 403 'Admin only'.
endpoints.notes: Read-only. 500 only if stats computation throws.
endpoints.result: Admin: GET /api/upload/stats -> 200 {"total_files":2,"total_size":697,"total_size_mb":0.0,"file_types":{"application/pdf":1,"image/png":1},"cleanup_days":30} (matches get_upload_stats). Unauthenticated -> 401 'Not authenticated'.

endpoints.purpose: Download an uploaded file by ID; ?thumb=1 returns a cached 320px JPEG thumbnail for images
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: POST /api/upload first as the same user; take files[0].id. Then curl -b cookies.txt http://HOST/api/upload/<id> -> 200 raw file bytes, Content-Type guessed from extension, Content-Disposition uses original filename. For an image, add ?thumb=1 -> 200 image/jpeg thumbnail (cached under UPLOAD_DIR/.thumbs/).
endpoints.bad_input: GET /api/upload/not-a-valid-id -> 400 'Invalid file ID' (must match ^[0-9a-fA-F]{32}\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$). Valid-format but nonexistent id (32 hex chars + .png) -> 404 'File not found'.
endpoints.notes: Ownership: when auth is configured, a non-owner non-admin gets 404; unauthenticated gets 403. Thumbnail generation needs Pillow; on failure falls through to full image. Walks UPLOAD_DIR tree to locate the file.
endpoints.result: GET /api/upload/aaf965e307cb4ce692c0918e5c6550e0.png -> 200 image/png 70B, Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="audit-tmp-red.png". ?thumb=1 -> 200 image/jpeg 634B (valid JPEG, 1x1, cached under .thumbs/). Bad input /api/upload/not-a-valid-id -> 400 'Invalid file ID'. Valid-format nonexistent /api/upload/0000...0000.png -> 404 'File not found'.

endpoints.purpose: Run the configured vision-language model on an uploaded image (OCR/description), cached on disk; force=1 recomputes
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: upload an image as the same user, take its id. curl -b cookies.txt http://HOST/api/upload/<id>/vision -> 200 {"text":"<description>","cached":false}; immediate second call -> {"cached":true}. ?force=1 recomputes (new model call). IMPORTANT: if vision is disabled or no vision model is configured, still 200 with placeholder text like '[No vision model configured — set one in Settings → Vision]' — no model call made.
endpoints.bad_input: Call it on a non-image upload (e.g. an uploaded .txt id) -> 400 'Not an image'. Invalid id format -> 400 'Invalid file ID'.
endpoints.notes: Consumes LLM/vision allowance on first call and on force=1 (analyze_image_with_vl in src/document_processor.py with vision fallback chain). Cache file: UPLOAD_DIR/.vision/{file_id}.txt. Owner/admin-only when auth configured (404 for others). 500 'Vision analysis failed: ...' if the model call throws.
endpoints.result: tiny png upload (files= field) -> vision: 200 {'text':'[No vision model configured — set one in Settings → Vision]','cached':false} = documented degraded path (quirk d)

endpoints.purpose: Persist user-edited vision/OCR text override for an attachment (written to the same vision cache file)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: upload a file as the same user (must exist in uploads.json). curl -X PUT -b cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"my corrected OCR text"}' http://HOST/api/upload/<id>/vision -> 200 {"ok":true}. Verify by GET .../vision -> {"text":"my corrected OCR text","cached":true}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"text": 123} -> 400 'text must be a string'. Valid-format unknown id -> 404 'File not found'.
endpoints.notes: No image-mime check on PUT (works on any owned upload). Owner/admin-only when auth configured. Subsequent chat sends pick this text up as the vision override.
endpoints.result: PUT /api/upload/aaf965e307cb4ce692c0918e5c6550e0.png/vision {"text":"audit-tmp corrected OCR text"} -> 200 {"ok":true}. Verified via GET .../vision -> 200 {"text":"audit-tmp corrected OCR text","cached":true} (served from cache, no LLM call). Bad input {"text":123} -> 400 'text must be a string'. Unknown valid-format id -> 404 'File not found'. Vision override cache file removed afterward.

endpoints.purpose: Synchronous (non-streaming) chat completion for external integrations (n8n/Make/Activepieces) using API-token auth
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: an active API token with "chat" scope (created via the api_token routes) AND at least one enabled ModelEndpoint with a non-"auto"-resolvable model, or pass api_key. curl -X POST /api/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer ody_<token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"message": "Say OK"}' → 200 {"response": "<assistant text>", "session_id": "<uuid>", "model": "<resolved model>"}. Alternative no-endpoint path: include "api_key": "<provider key>", "model": "deepseek-chat" (base_url auto-resolved from provider/model prefix).
endpoints.bad_input: Call with session cookie instead of bearer token → 403 "This endpoint requires an API token"; token without chat scope → 403 "API token is not scoped for chat"; {"message": "  "} → 400 "Message is required"; api_key with unrecognizable model and no base_url → 400 "Could not auto-detect provider...".
endpoints.notes: Consumes an LLM call (llm_call_async, 120s client timeout) BUT /api/v1/chat is NOT in app.py's 45s _TIMEOUT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES, so a slow model can yield 504 from the hard-timeout middleware. Side effects: creates/persists a session named "API Chat" owned by the token's owner; appends user+assistant messages; fires async "chat.completed" outbound webhook event. session resume path enforces token-owner==session-owner (404 otherwise). model "auto" triggers a 5s /models discovery call against the endpoint. Direct-api_key path hits external paid providers (deepseek/openai/groq/...) — EXTERNAL-CREDS flavored; the fallback path uses the locally configured endpoint.
endpoints.result: Bearer ody_ token, {'message':'Say OK'} -> {'response':'OK','session_id',...,'model':'claude-opus-4-8'}. NOTE: model 'auto' resolves to FIRST advertised model of first enabled endpoint (code-intended); recommendation: prefer configured default_model

endpoints.purpose: Return Vaultwarden/Bitwarden CLI config (server URL, email, unlocked flag, bw_installed) without secrets
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session: curl -b admin_cookies.txt http://HOST/api/vault/config -> 200 {"server_url":"","email":"","unlocked":false,"unlocked_at":"","bw_installed":false} on a clean install (bw_installed true only if the bw CLI is on PATH). Non-admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Runs 'bw --version' as a subprocess to compute bw_installed; safe without bw (returns false). Reads data/vault.json.
endpoints.result: Admin: GET /api/vault/config -> 200 {"server_url":"","email":"","unlocked":false,"unlocked_at":"","bw_installed":false} on clean install (no data/vault.json, bw not on PATH -> _check_bw_installed false). Re-confirmed cleared state after logout.

endpoints.purpose: Save Vaultwarden server URL + email; runs 'bw config server <url>' when URL non-empty
endpoints.test_plan: Happy path WITHOUT needing the bw CLI: curl -X POST -b admin_cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"server_url":"","email":"vault@example.com"}' http://HOST/api/vault/config -> 200 {"ok":true} (empty server_url skips the bw subprocess). With a non-empty server_url and no bw CLI installed -> 200 {"ok":false,"error":"bw config failed: bw CLI not installed..."}.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing required fields is impossible (both default to ""), but a non-JSON body -> 422 from Pydantic.
endpoints.notes: Side effect: writes data/vault.json (chmod 600 on POSIX). Errors are returned as HTTP 200 with ok:false — assert on the JSON body, not the status code.
endpoints.result: Admin: POST {"server_url":"","email":"audit-tmp@example.com"} -> 200 {"ok":true} (empty url skips bw, writes data/vault.json). POST {"server_url":"https://vault.example.com",...} -> 200 {"ok":false,"error":"bw config failed: bw CLI not installed..."} and correctly did NOT persist server_url (vault.json still server_url:""). Bad input non-JSON body -> 422 (json_invalid). Assert on JSON body not status (errors are 200+ok:false by design).

endpoints.purpose: Lock the vault: clear stored session from data/vault.json and run 'bw lock'
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session, no body: curl -X POST -b admin_cookies.txt http://HOST/api/vault/lock -> 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Vault locked"}. Always succeeds — the 'bw lock' subprocess result is ignored, so this is testable without bw CLI or any vault setup.
endpoints.notes: Idempotent; pops session/unlocked_at keys from data/vault.json.
endpoints.result: Admin: POST /api/vault/lock (no body) -> 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Vault locked"}. Idempotent; pops session/unlocked_at, 'bw lock' subprocess result ignored so testable without bw CLI.

endpoints.purpose: Log in to Vaultwarden via 'bw login <email> --raw', storing the session key on success
endpoints.test_plan: Requires bw CLI installed AND a reachable Vaultwarden account: curl -X POST -b admin_cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"vault@example.com","master_password":"correct-horse"}' http://HOST/api/vault/login -> 200 {"ok":true} (or {"ok":true,"already":true} if already logged in). Without bw CLI: 200 {"ok":false,"error":"Login failed: bw CLI not installed..."} — that ok:false path is the realistic smoke test in a credless environment.
endpoints.bad_input: Body missing master_password -> 422 validation error.
endpoints.notes: Spawns bw subprocess, pipes password to stdin. Saves email (always) and session+unlocked_at (on success) to data/vault.json. Failures return HTTP 200 with ok:false. Won't capture session if account has 2FA.
endpoints.result: EXTERNAL-CREDS, bw CLI not installed + no Vaultwarden account. Admin POST {"email":"audit-tmp@example.com","master_password":"dummy-not-real"} -> 200 {"ok":false,"error":"Login failed: bw CLI not installed (install nodejs-bitwarden-cli or bitwarden-cli)"} -- clean error, no 500/traceback/hang (FileNotFoundError caught in _run_bw -> rc 127). Bad input: missing master_password -> 422. Cannot exercise success path without bw CLI + credentials.

endpoints.purpose: Run 'bw logout' and clear session+email from the stored vault config
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session, no body: curl -X POST -b admin_cookies.txt http://HOST/api/vault/logout -> 200 {"ok":true}. Always succeeds regardless of bw CLI presence (subprocess result ignored).
endpoints.notes: Side effect: removes session, email, unlocked_at from data/vault.json; subsequent GET /api/vault/config shows email:"" and unlocked:false. Run vault tests in order: config -> lock/logout last.
endpoints.result: Admin: POST /api/vault/logout (no body) -> 200 {"ok":true}. Side effect verified: subsequent GET /api/vault/config showed email:"" (session/email/unlocked_at popped). 'bw logout' subprocess result ignored so succeeds without bw CLI.

endpoints.purpose: Unlock the vault via 'bw unlock <password> --raw' and persist the BW_SESSION key
endpoints.test_plan: Requires bw CLI + prior login: curl -X POST -b admin_cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"master_password":"correct-horse"}' http://HOST/api/vault/unlock -> 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Vault unlocked"}. Without bw CLI: 200 {"ok":false,"error":"Unlock failed: bw CLI not installed..."}.
endpoints.bad_input: {} -> 422 (master_password required).
endpoints.notes: WARNING: master password is passed as a subprocess argv (visible in process list). Stores session in data/vault.json. HTTP 200 with ok:false on failure.
endpoints.result: EXTERNAL-CREDS, bw CLI not installed. Admin POST {"master_password":"dummy-not-real"} -> 200 {"ok":false,"error":"Unlock failed: bw CLI not installed (install nodejs-bitwarden-cli or bitwarden-cli)"} -- clean error, no 500/traceback/hang. Bad input: {} -> 422 (master_password required). Cannot exercise success path without bw CLI + prior login.

endpoints.purpose: Return application version string
endpoints.test_plan: curl http://localhost:PORT/api/version → 200 {"version": "0.9.1"} (APP_VERSION from core/constants.py). No auth, no fixtures.

endpoints.purpose: List all registered outbound webhooks (secrets never returned, only has_secret)
endpoints.test_plan: As admin: GET /api/webhooks → 200 JSON array (possibly []) of {id, name, url, has_secret, events[], is_active, last_triggered_at, last_status_code, last_error, created_at}.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session → 403 "Admin only".
endpoints.notes: require_admin passes when AUTH_ENABLED=false, auth unconfigured fails with 403, internal-tool header bypasses.
endpoints.result: Admin cookie: GET /api/webhooks -> 200 JSON array. After creating fixture, returned full documented shape: {id,name,url,has_secret:false,events:["chat.completed"],is_active:true,last_triggered_at,last_status_code,last_error,created_at}. Bad input: no cookie -> 401 {"error":"Not authenticated"} (upstream auth middleware fires before route). Non-admin 403 path is enforced by _require_admin (core/middleware.py:20) called as the first statement in webhook_routes.py:38; not exercised with a live non-admin session to preserve the shared single-login budget, but gate is demonstrably active (401 on unauth).

endpoints.purpose: Register an outbound webhook (name, url, optional secret, comma-separated events)
endpoints.test_plan: FORM-encoded (not JSON): curl -X POST /api/webhooks -d 'name=CI hook' -d 'url=https://example.com/hook' -d 'events=chat.completed' → 200 {"id": "<8-char>", "name": "CI hook"}. Allowed events: session.created, chat.completed, chat.message, webhook.test.
endpoints.bad_input: events=bogus → 400 "Invalid events: bogus. Allowed: ..."; url=http://127.0.0.1/x or any private/internal address → 400 "URL must not point to private/internal addresses"; empty name → 400 "Webhook name is required".
endpoints.notes: Form fields, application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Secret encrypted at rest via api_key_manager Fernet (plaintext fallback if unavailable). SSRF guard rejects private nets — use a public URL like https://example.com for happy path; deliveries to it will just fail harmlessly.
endpoints.result: Form-encoded (application/x-www-form-urlencoded): name=audit-tmp hook, url=https://example.com/hook, events=chat.completed -> 200 {"id":"2410eed2","name":"audit-tmp hook"}; confirmed persisted via GET. Bad inputs all correct: events=bogus -> 400 {"detail":"Invalid events: bogus. Allowed: chat.completed, chat.message, session.created"}; url=http://127.0.0.1/x -> 400 {"detail":"URL must not point to private/internal addresses"} (SSRF guard, webhook_manager.py validate_webhook_url); empty name -> 400 {"detail":"Webhook name is required"}.

endpoints.purpose: Delete one registered webhook
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: throwaway webhook. DELETE /api/webhooks/<id> → 200 {"status": "deleted"}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id → 404 "Webhook not found".
endpoints.result: DELETE /api/webhooks/2410eed2 (admin) -> 200 {"status":"deleted"}; subsequent GET /api/webhooks -> [] confirming removal. Bad input: DELETE /api/webhooks/nonexist9 -> 404 {"detail":"Webhook not found"} (delete count 0 -> raise, webhook_routes.py:142-143).

endpoints.purpose: Toggle a webhook's is_active flag (no body — pure toggle)

endpoints.purpose: Send a webhook.test delivery to the registered URL
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: webhook created via POST /api/webhooks. POST /api/webhooks/<id>/test → 200 {"status": "sent"} regardless of whether the remote URL accepted it (delivery result lands in last_status_code/last_error on the next GET /api/webhooks).

Endpoint contract (return sent regardless of remote outcome, result lands in last_status_code/last_error) is satisfied. Bad input: POST /api/webhooks/nonexist9/test -> 404 {"detail":"Webhook not found"}.

endpoints.purpose: OpenAI-compatible chat completions shim: renders messages+tool schemas into a prompt, spawns the local `claude -p` CLI subprocess, and translates output (including a sentinel-based tool-call protocol) back into OpenAI completion / SSE chunk format
endpoints.test_plan: Non-streaming happy path: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8750/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5","stream":false,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the single word: pong"}]}' -> 200 JSON with object="chat.completion", id starting "chatcmpl-", choices[0].message.role="assistant", choices[0].message.content non-empty, finish_reason="stop", and usage.prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens integers. Streaming variant: same body with "stream":true -> 200 text/event-stream of `data: {...chat.completion.chunk...}` lines (first delta {"role":"assistant"}, then content deltas, optional reasoning_content deltas, `: keepalive` SSE comments during silence), a choices=[] usage chunk, then byte-exact `data: [DONE]`. Tool-call path: include "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_time","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"tz":{"type":"string"}},"required":["tz"]}}}] and a prompt that needs it -> finish_reason="tool_calls" with message.tool_calls[0].function.name/arguments (JSON-string args). Fixture: claude CLI (>= v2.1.161) on PATH or CLAUDE_BIN set, AND logged in via subscription/OAuth (`claude` login) — otherwise expect 401.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-JSON body (e.g. curl -d 'not json' -H 'Content-Type: application/json') -> 400 {"error":{"message":"invalid JSON body"}}. Also: with claude logged out -> 401 "claude: authentication failed"; allowance exhausted -> 429; subprocess garbage/exit -> 502; exceeding HARD_CAP (300s) -> 504 "claude: timed out" (non-streaming) or stream truncation.
endpoints.notes: Consumes the user's Claude subscription allowance on every call — budget test runs accordingly. Spawns one `claude -p --strict-mcp-config` subprocess per request with cwd=/tmp/odysseus-claude-sidecar (CLAUDE_SIDECAR_CWD), prompt fed via stdin; subprocess killed on client disconnect, own process group SIGKILLed on escalation. Concurrency gated by an asyncio.Semaphore of CLAUDE_SIDECAR_CONCURRENCY (default 6); slot released on subprocess exit via a guard task, force-released at the 300s hard cap. Streaming pre-content failures (no first text delta within FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT, default 90s) return HTTP non-200 JSON instead of SSE so Odysseus fallback engages. Claude gets native read-only fallback tools Read,Glob,Grep,WebSearch,WebFetch,Skill (CLAUDE_SIDECAR_NATIVE_TOOLS; set "" for pure reasoning). System prompt is prefixed with an Odysseus runtime preamble unless CLAUDE_SIDECAR_PREAMBLE=0. Unknown model strings are passed straight to `claude --model`, so an invalid model surfaces as a 502/4xx from the CLI, not request validation. Side effect: writes Claude session .jsonl files under ~/.claude/projects/<scratch-slug>/.
endpoints.result: non-streaming 'say ok'->'ok' (after fix 9b8061c); streaming SSE chunks+[DONE]; tools sentinel->native delta.tool_calls finish_reason=tool_calls.
